CFML Language Reference: Tags

CFABORT

CFABORT ends the request right where it stands. Everything generated so far is sent to the browser; nothing after the tag runs. With SHOWERROR it stops the page with an error instead.

Category

Flow control

Syntax

<CFABORT SHOWERROR="error message">

Attributes

SHOWERROR
Optional. Message to show. The page then ends with an Application error that carries this message, just as if an error had occurred, and it can be caught with CFTRY/CFCATCH.

Usage

A plain CFABORT is not an error: CFTRY does not catch it, and error handlers set with CFERROR are not called. Note that OnRequestEnd.cfm is not run either, so anything it would add to the page is lost.

Remember to close any open HTML tables before aborting: Netscape 4 shows nothing at all of a table that never ends. CFABORT is handy inside Application.cfm to stop unauthorized visitors after showing them a login form.

Example

Opens the example in a new window. The example runs on this server, so it only works when you browse from the server itself (127.0.0.1).
<!--- Pay employees in order of seniority until the budget runs out --->
<CFSET Budget = 500000>
<CFSET Spent = 0>
<CFQUERY NAME="Staff" DATASOURCE="cfsnippets">
SELECT FirstName, LastName, Salary FROM Employees ORDER BY StartDate
</CFQUERY>

<TABLE BORDER=1 CELLPADDING=3>
<TR><TH>Employee</TH><TH>Salary</TH><TH>Spent so far</TH></TR>
<CFLOOP QUERY="Staff">
  <CFIF Spent + Salary GT Budget>
    </TABLE>
    <CFOUTPUT><P><B>Budget of #DollarFormat(Budget)# exhausted at row #CurrentRow#.
    #FirstName# #LastName# and the rest will have to wait.</B></P></CFOUTPUT>
    <CFABORT>
  </CFIF>
  <CFSET Spent = Spent + Salary>
  <CFOUTPUT><TR><TD>#FirstName# #LastName#</TD><TD>#DollarFormat(Salary)#</TD><TD>#DollarFormat(Spent)#</TD></TR></CFOUTPUT>
</CFLOOP>
</TABLE>
<P>Everybody got paid. (You will not see this line: the budget is too small.)</P>
